purpose: Working deployable opinionated reference application; research-driven core capability, reliability, usability and reproducibility improvements. Not a competing commercial SaaS or a benchmark-score target.
publication_boundary: Explicit public allowlist: published sources and authorized maintainer engineering summaries only. Original private case verdicts/discussions/artifacts are not exported.

records.title: Unsupported data must not become a false zero
records.research_source: Published unsupported-data Result: https://aidemos.com/benchmarks/ai-database-agents/results/futuresmart-ai-database-agent/the-connected-data-cannot-answer-the-question. Separate maintainer reproduction/validation, not an exact historical rerun.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Published Fail, unchanged; separate released engineering fix does not regrade the original run.
records.observed_failure: An unsupported reviews question was answered with zero using unrelated audit records.
records.root_cause: SQL could run on an available table even when that table did not represent the requested metric. Query success was mistaken for answer support.
records.engineering_decision: Require an explicit schema-support decision. Keep genuine zero distinct from unavailable data; preserve table-access and execution-error guards.
records.implementation: Added answerability propagation through SQL generation/execution, final answer and multi-source paths. Clear surrogate SQL/stale rows when unsupported.
records.validation: Focused regressions cover unsupported input, real zero, positive results, denied tables and execution errors. Independent staged browser controls covered missing data, count 0 and count 2; a production missing-data check and a separate real-source positive SQL/rows/chart check passed.
records.limits: A bounded product fix, not a full historical benchmark rerun. Metadata/schema-hint omissions remain separate. The original research verdict is not changed.

records.title: Render nested stacked-chart results without losing series
records.research_source: Published charting context: https://aidemos.com/tools/futuresmart-ai-database-agent. The exact nested-renderer defect was a separate maintainer reproduction.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Published Automatic Chart Generation: Partial, unchanged; exact nested-renderer scenario is not the published historical test
records.observed_failure: A valid nested stacked-chart response could be unavailable in the UI despite valid SQL/rows and stored chart data.
records.root_cause: The frontend result contract did not consistently normalize flat and nested segmented chart shapes.
records.engineering_decision: Normalize the supplied result contract; keep individual values, zeros, missing series and Data/Query/Raw views. Do not replace SQL or tune a model to repair a renderer.
records.implementation: Updated typed chart normalization and stacked-bar rendering for live and saved conversations.
records.validation: Component contracts and independent staged/production browser checks passed. A synthetic four-order source produced visible North 100+150 and South 80+120 segments; SQL, all rows and full-reload saved reopen agreed.
records.limits: This fixes rendering. It does not prove that a chart-only follow-up preserves the original business metric, or upgrade the published broad charting result.

records.title: Preserve metric meaning when changing scope
records.research_source: Unpublished researcher feedback retained privately; published follow-up context is linked in baseline.md.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Not publicly verifiable: case-level source is unpublished; no new benchmark verdict
records.observed_failure: Maintainer replays found numerator/population and scope inconsistencies; a plausible percentage could represent a different question.
records.root_cause: Metric definition, denominator population and follow-up scope were not consistently preserved. Exact historical deployed configuration is unknown.
records.engineering_decision: Keep numerator/denominator and scope guards explicit. Compare to reference SQL on the same data state; never force historical numeric literals onto a changed database.
records.implementation: A separate candidate adds metric/scope consistency checks; it remains outside the accepted main application.
records.validation: Native pair/grouped controls passed after earlier wrong results were retained. Remaining semantic controls, independent candidate browser acceptance and production proof are incomplete.
records.limits: No release or historical benchmark Pass. This candidate is separate from the delivery work.

records.title: Deliver and save the primary answer before optional work
records.research_source: Maintainer-observed timeout/empty initial UI and measured request-path investigation; no published case-level research result established.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Not publicly verifiable: case-level source is unpublished; no new benchmark verdict
records.observed_failure: The old request waited for the whole graph/chart before its first useful answer. Later transport errors could erase an already received answer or identity.
records.root_cause: Required answer delivery, optional work, persistence acknowledgement and frontend error state shared one fragile completion boundary.
records.engineering_decision: Use one owned request lifecycle; publish an immutable validated primary after existing guards, acknowledge one insert, and scope optional updates by actual row and authorized ownership. Never retry an insert after unknown commit.
records.implementation: A separate candidate implements primary-before-optional delivery, scoped persistence, retained frontend identity/answer, bounded cancellation and saved-answer-status replay. It does not change models or hosted edge timeouts.
records.validation: On one independent real-provider synthetic sales turn, saved answer arrived 10.922 seconds, chart/EOF 14.500 seconds; complete two rows and saved reopen matched the source. Six native lifecycle contracts passed with declared upstream stubs/no provider calls. A native TCP-reset UI check retained the answer and obtained SQL/rows via one automatic saved read.
records.limits: These timings are not a before/after speed comparison, p95 or SaaS accuracy result. With debug disabled, primary wire has no SQL/rows; they reconcile from storage. The reset proxy cannot exclude coalesced later frames, so exclusive-primary-only delivery is not claimed. Final saved-status correction has green CI but independent replay is incomplete. No production promotion.

records.title: Preserve a complete installable reference application
records.research_source: Maintainer installation/repository review, not a benchmark accuracy case.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Not publicly verifiable: case-level source is unpublished; no new benchmark verdict
records.observed_failure: A working service repository was still cluttered and depended on deployment knowledge rather than a clear complete-product installation.
records.root_cause: Product source, installation assets and internal operational material were mixed.
records.engineering_decision: Keep backend, UI, supported deployment, sample and guides in one opinionated repository. Preserve existing behavior; keep private operational history out of distributable builds.
records.implementation: Reorganized source and added a supported one-clone installation and deployment documentation.
records.validation: Fresh-checkout build, UI/API sample checks and restart/persistence were independently checked. The then-known chart limitation was recorded and fixed separately in DA-002.
records.limits: Installability is not general answer accuracy, public licensing, or proven load capacity.

records.title: Evaluate speed together with correctness
records.research_source: Maintainer operation timings and separately controlled local evaluations; unpublished dataset/context details stay private.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Not publicly verifiable: case-level source is unpublished; no new benchmark verdict
records.observed_failure: Faster responses could contain wrong SQL, wrong populations or unsupported units, while some provider requests were rejected.
records.root_cause: Two production observations spent 37.083 s of 43.037 s and 72.556 s of 83.958 s in SQL generation, with SQL execution of 0.029 s / 0.030 s. This does not isolate a universal provider cause.
records.engineering_decision: Compare complete typed rows to pinned business definitions, use finite call budgets and retain every refusal/wrong result. Do not choose a model from speed alone or claim unverified remote experiment persistence.
records.implementation: Separate evaluation code and sanitized local result records were prepared; no winning model was adopted.
records.validation: Reviewed complete SQL/results and local evaluator feedback; no accepted quality winner. Remote experiment persistence remained unverified after rate limits; polling stopped.
records.limits: No cost-saving, TTFT, p95, generic model-capability, or broad accuracy claim; failed screens remain failed.

records.title: Core capability quality takes precedence over commercial feature parity
records.research_source: Project-purpose decision from the maintainer; recorded in the README.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Not publicly verifiable: case-level source is unpublished; no new benchmark verdict
records.observed_failure: Treating every capability row as a feature promise would replace a dependable reference application with an unbounded commercial roadmap.
records.root_cause: Capability availability, correctness, usability and measurement are different evaluation dimensions.
records.engineering_decision: Prioritize correct SQL/results, inspectability, reproducibility and usable deployment. Generalized multi-tenant controls, billing expansion and feature-for-feature SaaS competition are outside the current objective.
records.implementation: Documentation decision only; no runtime capability removed or implied to exist.
records.validation: Reviewed against the existing product boundary and this history. Missing capabilities retain their original private verdicts.
records.limits: Deferred capabilities do not become benchmark Pass results or disappear from the private baseline.

records.engineering_decision: Compare complete typed rows with explicit column association, multiplicity/order/numeric/NULL/unit policies; use a conservative bounded demo narrative checker. Preserve the small install demo and add a separate fixed relational regression fixture.

records.title: Use one OpenAI credential for default query and chart operations
records.research_source: Engineering observation; no new published benchmark run
records.observed_failure: Default operations require several model providers, making installation and hosted operation depend on multiple provider credentials.
records.root_cause: Multiple-provider defaults were confirmed. In the controlled OpenAI-only attempt, the configured credential was denied gpt-6-luna at the router (OpenAI PermissionDeniedError, model_not_found); SQL generation and charting were not reached. At that first-attempt checkpoint, the reason for unavailability was unestablished. A subsequent authenticated read of the bound project showed the selected IDs absent from its seven-entry allowlist; the independently verified additive correction is recorded below. The later chart attempt independently exposed a selection/policy mismatch: the direct-description selector included an excluded table, and the pre-sampling policy guard correctly denied it. This is separate from the earlier provider denial.
records.engineering_decision: Use gpt-6.1-sol low for database/table selection, SQL generation/correction and transformation planning; gpt-6-luna none for routine operations. Preserve existing embedding models and vectors.
records.implementation: Candidate OpenAI model defaults and SDK endpoint/reasoning compatibility, with a narrow identity-bound pre-sampling gate. Legacy-release integer0/1 flags are accepted only through an explicit compatibility lane; strict current access-policy semantics remain unchanged. Prompts, output schemas and embedding vectors are preserved.
records.validation: Offline SDK transport/parse controls and independent emitted-node access controls passed. Required CI39614280096 on020d808 passed. First CI39613323118 exposed a new test-only checkout/image path error; original failure retained and corrected with the established resolver. Controlled runtime192 became healthy, then the first ordinary API query returned HTTP500 after4.5s. Actual request stack reached OpenAI router and was denied gpt-6-luna/model_not_found. The client JSONDecodeError was a secondary500 parsing symptom. The remaining chart query was withheld; no retry or alternative-model query occurred. Subsequent explicitly authorized administrative remediation used an existing Admin credential and independently bound the actual runtime project/key. Its allowlist kept all seven existing IDs and added only gpt-6-luna, gpt-6.1-sol and retained text-embedding-3-large. Admin readback and same-runtime-key catalog show all three; no inference or deployment ran during this administrative correction. After administrative remediation, the one remaining authorized chart submission ran on the unchanged immutable candidate. It returned HTTP500 plaintext after11.593s. Exact-request logs show description-based selection returned orders and order_status_history against a temporary orders-only policy; the pre-sampling guard rejected the excluded table with TableAccessPolicyError. No retry occurred; both authorized submissions are spent.
records.limits: No successful query, chart, live UI, saved-result reopen, accuracy or benchmark Pass. For the first attempt, HTTP content type/response-header request ID were not retained and remain unknown. No billing/funding, organization-verification or global model-availability diagnosis is claimed. Previous deployment191 and exact original selected-agent context settings were restored; other144 stored overrides were unchanged. Source candidate remains unaccepted end to end. Administrative access correction does not change the original failed runtime result or establish current product success. For the separate second attempt, HTTP content type was retained as text/plain; charset=utf-8, while a response-header request ID was not retained. Original metadata was independently restored; final compute closeout is independently accepted: original191 stable and candidate193 STOPPED21:45:51.239IST. No chart/SQL/model-quality success is established by this scope denial.
